meta.provenance_note: Seven lessons per unit, transcribed 2026-09-10 from the student book itself. Each unit prints exactly seven «LESSON nA» page headers (1A..7A, 18pt), each carrying a skill banner and, after a «|», a topic label when the book gives one; and each lesson prints exactly one «□ I can …» statement, 35 per semester = 5 units × 7. Lesson identity and order come from those headers, and the «I can» statement is the lesson's outcome, held verbatim in objectives[]. Same Pearson «Jordan High Note» series and same format as the Grade 8 and Grade 9 English books, which this repo already models the same way (see iqra_curriculum_g9_eng_sem1.json). The two-page 'Contents' scope-and-sequence spread (PDF pages 4-5; columns UNIT, GRAMMAR, VOCABULARY, READING, LISTENING, SPEAKING, WRITING) is still carried in the six *_topic / writing_task fields, with the book's own page references intact — but distributed onto the lesson whose printed pages each entry names, which is how «p6 Appearance, clothes, footwear and accessories» lands on LESSON 2A VOCABULARY | Appearance instead of on the whole unit. Arabic titles and topic labels are OUR OWN TRANSLATIONS: this book is English-only and prints no Arabic beyond its cover. Only unit titles and skill banners are translated; topic labels and every «I can» outcome stay verbatim in English, because translating an outcome changes what a teacher is told the lesson delivers — the same treatment recorded in the Grade 8/9 English files and the four vocational English catalogs.

source_books.student_book_s1: كتاب الطالب لمادة اللغة الإنجليزية الصف العاشر الفصل الأول.pdf — 78 pages, sourceId eng-s1-student-book. Contents spread: pages 4-5.

known_gaps: Unit 5's LESSON 2A and LESSON 3A share printed page 50 — VOCABULARY | Phrasal verbs related to studying on the left, GRAMMAR opening on the right and running on to page 51. An earlier version of this file cited that as the reason a seven-lesson breakdown could not be derived, and cited it as page 52, which is the PDF page, not the printed one. It does not block anything: each slot still prints exactly one «I can» («I can talk about studying.» on p50, «I can use the Future Continuous and the Future Perfect …» on p51), which is why lessons are counted by «I can» statements rather than by pages. The scope-and-sequence cells for that page separate the same way — the vocabulary column's «p50 Phrasal verbs related to studying» is LESSON 2A's own banner text, and the grammar column's «pp50-51 Future Continuous and Future Perfect» is LESSON 3A's.

No نتاجات التعلم boxes. This series prints none of the Arabic learning-outcome lists the science student books carry; what it prints instead is one «□ I can …» statement per lesson, and that is what objectives[] holds. So the outcomes here are the book's own words, not invented — but they are not NCCD نتاجات and should not be read as such.
No period counts. The teacher's guide, which is where the science books' periods come from, is not in the repo for English.

vocabulary[] is empty everywhere. This book scatters its words through the lesson exercises and the Word List on pp62-66 rather than printing a terms box on the lesson opener; transcribing them means reading the exercises, not the page header — the same gap recorded in the Grade 8 and Grade 9 English files.

The LIFE SKILLS spreads (after units 2 and 4) print no «LESSON nA» header and no «I can», so they are not lessons. Each is kept in the life_skill field of the last lesson of the unit it follows — the lesson it is printed immediately after — so that its title and pages stay in the catalog rather than being dropped; it is not a claim that the spread belongs to that lesson. The end matter — Culture Spot pp58-59, Literature Spot pp60-61, Word List pp62-66, Grammar Reference pp67-71, Irregular Verbs p72, Communication pp73-75 — is not modelled at all.
